panels.title: Ingestion Budget Usage by Tenant (Daily, per Signal)
panels.description: Each tenant/signal's real ingested volume since local midnight (Europe/Zurich), as a percentage of that SIGNAL's own daily budget - both read directly from two gauges scripts/ingestion-midnight-snapshot.py pushes every 2 minutes, demo_ingestion_since_midnight{signal=...,tenant=...} and demo_ingestion_daily_budget{signal=...,tenant=...} - no subtraction on this panel's own side at all. NFR-05 SECOND pre-test audit round, fixed here: this used to recompute "current counter value minus a separately-pushed day-start snapshot" in this panel's OWN PromQL, independently of (and able to silently disagree with) whatever the enforcer script itself was internally deciding to throttle on, with its own version of that script's pre-fix reset-insensitivity (a raw subtraction, no per-series reset compensation, unlike what the enforcer's own since-midnight computation now does via Mimir's increase()). Both this panel and the enforcer now read the exact same, already-correct value. NFR-05 FIRST round finding, fixed then: this used to be one line per TENANT, summing all four signals into a single blended percentage against one combined budget - which mixed genuinely different bases (Loki/Tempo's real uncompressed bytes, Pyroscope's real but COMPRESSED bytes, Mimir's pure sample-count estimate, since it has no byte counter at all) as if they were one unit. Now one line per tenant PER SIGNAL, each against its own independent budget - Metrics (Mimir), Logs (Loki), Traces (Tempo), Profiles (Pyroscope). This is a genuine running total, not a smoothed instantaneous rate - it can only go up until the next real midnight. A tenant with no data yet for a given signal (e.g. never sent profiles) simply has no line for that signal, rather than a fabricated 0% entry.

panels.title: Ingestion Rate vs. Limit - Mimir (samples/sec)
panels.description: Which tenants' Mimir traffic is currently at or above the shared generic rate limit (scripts/provision.py's GENERIC_INGESTION_RATE_MB, same for every tenant) - a tenant's line crossing above the flat limit line means it's actively being throttled right now (see the Discard Rate panel below for confirmation). Native units, no conversion needed - both series come directly from Mimir's own metrics.

panels.title: Ingestion Rate vs. Limit - Loki (bytes/sec)
panels.description: Which tenants' Loki traffic is currently at or above the shared generic rate limit. Loki doesn't export its own configured limit as a metric, so the limit line is derived from Mimir's own exported limit (cortex_limits_overrides, converted *1000, the same ~1KB/sample assumption compute_overrides() itself uses) - accurate since every system shares the same configured generic value.

panels.title: Ingestion Rate vs. Limit - Tempo (bytes/sec)
panels.description: Which tenants' Tempo traffic is currently at or above the shared generic rate limit. Tempo doesn't export its own configured limit as a metric, so the limit line is derived from Mimir's own exported limit the same way as the Loki panel.

panels.title: Ingestion Rate vs. Limit - Pyroscope (bytes/sec)
panels.description: Which tenants' Pyroscope traffic is currently at or above the shared generic rate limit. Pyroscope doesn't export its own configured limit as a metric, so the limit line is derived from Mimir's own exported limit the same way as the Loki panel.

panels.title: Discard Rate - Mimir (samples/sec, by reason)
panels.description: Which tenants are actually having Mimir samples rejected right now, and why - the real consequence of the rate panel above. Once the ingestion-midnight-snapshot enforcer throttles a tenant for crossing its daily budget (see the top panel), its discards show up here too under reason=rate_limited - indistinguishable from an ordinary momentary burst over the generic per-second limit, since both go through the same native rate limiter.

panels.title: Discard Rate - Loki (bytes/sec, by reason)
panels.description: Which tenants are actually having Loki bytes rejected right now, and why.

panels.title: Discard Rate - Tempo (spans/sec, by reason)
panels.description: Which tenants are actually having Tempo spans rejected right now, and why. Tempo only exposes a discarded-spans counter (tempo_discarded_spans_total), not bytes - no byte-size-per-span assumption exists anywhere else in this repo to base a conversion on, so this stays in its native unit rather than a fabricated bytes estimate. Pyroscope has no equivalent panel - it exposes no discard counter at all; a rejection there is only visible as a client-side HTTP 429, not a metric.
